correctness.rationale: Exact finite-path vacancy recurrence yields per-edge probability e^{-t}u_i(v)u_{n-i}(v), uniformly summable to mean e^{-2-x}. Earliest-clock dependency chains are strictly decreasing, with probability at most 2/R! beyond radius R. Truncation with R=ceil(3 log n), factorial-moment independence of disjoint windows and near-tuple O(R/n) bounds establish Poisson(e^{-2-x}); saturation equals no available edge. Poisson martingale maximal inequality transfers Gumbel from time to discrete attempts. The standalone verifier reproduced 6154 finite exact identities and controlled numerical checks, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The classic first-order T_n/(n log n) result leaves order-n fluctuations unspecified. The exact limit, including the nontrivial shift two, provides a genuinely motivated sharp distributional description of the jamming latency for one of the standard one-dimensional RSA models. Poissonization and rare-window dependence control are substantive mathematical mechanisms.
